chapter: Leading the band after Chick Webb, 1939-40
title: Bill Beeson takes Chick's drum chair
summary: The band returns to the Savoy briefly; senior men run it, with Chick's friend Bill Beeson on drums, though no one could fill Chick's place.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: And then we, you know, come back to the Savoy Ballroom. No, I think it was about a week later (inaudible) went back to the ballroom -- the Savoy Ballroom for a couple of (inaudible) days, you know.
And we were getting ready to go -- to finish the trip. Because, you know, we were booked up all the way down into Florida and all through the

Middle West, and things like that. Those dates were still pending.

And they decided to -- we put Bill Beeson on drums and (inaudible) the band up. I wasn't running the band that time. I think Taft, Jordon and Edgar Sampson -- couple of (inaudible), you know, just the top men in the band (inaudible) running the band (inaudible).
It was their decision to put Beeson in on drums?
Yeah. Well, Beeson was a drummer who was very close to Chick Webb. He was always around all the time and he used to hang out with Chick a lot.
He didn't drum anything like Chick. He had his own style, you know. Chick was a (inaudible) drummer. You know, Chick would play all types of (inaudible).
Bill Beeson was a very good drummer, but it's very hard to put anybody, you know, just to find somebody and say, well, we'll put this drummer in Chick's place.
